sections.name: Kritter
sections.card:
Summary: The Kremling Krew's foot soldiers. In Donkey Kong 64 they are simply called Kremlings, and each wears a sleeveless leather jacket, with a skull and crossbones across its back.
Weak points: Despite their muscular look, they are usually the weakest of the Kremlings.
Tips: You meet them on Crocodile Isle and in every world except Fungi Forest and Creepy Castle. In Frantic Factory a red kind belches in a set order, and Lanky has to memorize it and repeat it to earn a Golden Banana.

sections.name: Klump
sections.card:
Summary: A pink Kremling in a yellow-orange vest. It lobs unripe green oranges at whichever Kong you are playing, and it can also knock a Kong backward with a belly bump.
Weak points: Klumps resist basic attacks, and a direct hit only stuns one for a while. Besides the shockwave attack, a thrown orange or an instrument move, the only way to really finish one is for Chunky to touch it while in his Hunky Chunky form.
Tips: A beaten Klump salutes, falls over and leaves three oranges. They show up in every level apart from Frantic Factory, Creepy Castle and the DK Isles hub. In Fungi Forest they are there only by day, and Skeleton Kremlings take over after dark.

sections.name: Kasplat
sections.card:
Summary: A big, muscular Kremling in a leather jacket and sunglasses that guards a blueprint. It slams the ground to send out a shockwave and can punch a Kong that comes close.
Weak points: Kasplats are tough and often take several hits, but a Kong's shockwave attack or instrument move beats one in a single hit, and so do five oranges. Chunky can flatten one in Hunky Chunky mode, but then it drops no blueprint.
Tips: Its hair colour shows which Kong can take its blueprint (yellow Donkey, red Diddy, blue Lanky, purple Tiny, green Chunky), and the hair turns white once the blueprint is taken. Hideout Helm has no Kasplats; every other level has five.

sections.name: Zinger
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow flying enemy. Some dive at the active Kong the moment they see it, while others let unripe green oranges fall once they spot you.
Weak points: An orange, an instrument move or a projectile shot defeats a Zinger. The ones that drop oranges generally respawn after you beat them, and the dive-bombers do not.
Tips: They appear on DK Isles and in Jungle Japes, Angry Aztec, Gloomy Galleon, Crystal Caves and, by day only, Fungi Forest, where bats replace them at night. Frantic Factory has robotic Mechanical Zingers instead, and in Angry Aztec a beaten Zinger that falls into the sand burns up and leaves no melon slice.

sections.name: Mad Jack
sections.card:
Summary: Frantic Factory's boss, the third in the game: a huge jack-in-the-box made of metal. Tiny Kong fights him on a floor of 16 glowing tiles.
Weak points: Pound the switch on the tile that matches the tile Mad Jack stands on with a Simian Slam to electrocute him, and five hits end the fight. The other switch shocks Tiny instead and costs her half a Watermelon of health.
Tips: While he hops, glide between tiles with Pony Tail Twirl, since he cannot hop diagonally. After the fourth hit he turns invisible, so follow the sparkles he leaves as he jumps. Falling off the stage does not lose the fight: a tile on the lower floor lifts Tiny back.

sections.name: Puftoss
sections.card:
Summary: The boss of Gloomy Galleon, a huge pufferfish. Lanky Kong fights it from a small coconut-half motorboat in a pool, after 250 bananas have been fed to Scoff to open the boss door.
Weak points: Drive the boat through all five DK stars before each one's timer runs out to bring electric poles up from the water, which shock Puftoss. A fifth hit defeats him.
Tips: The star timers start at 30 seconds and shrink to 25, 20, 15 and finally 10 in later rounds. Puftoss cannot hurt Lanky by touching him, but he spits fireballs, and in round two his water slams make shockwaves that vanish when they touch an electric pole.

sections.name: King Kut Out
sections.card:
Summary: Creepy Castle's boss, the seventh and next-to-last in the game: a rough cardboard cut-out of King K. Rool run by two Kritters. You fight it outdoors in a rainstorm, inside a square castle rampart.
Weak points: Get into the Barrel Cannon that points at it and fire yourself at the boss. The ninth hit destroys it and the Boss Key drops in the middle of the arena.
Tips: A shot with bad timing blasts the Kong out of the arena for good, and the next Kong comes out of the Tag Barrel (by default Tiny, then Chunky, Donkey and Diddy after Lanky). After the third hit a darker decoy follows it from the opposite wall, and blasting at the decoy throws you out. After three more hits it moves faster, so fire just as it appears in front of you; the ghosts that spawn near the cannons can be beaten to regain health.

sections.name: Golden Banana
sections.card:
Summary: Donkey Kong's own supply of bananas from his hoard, which the Kremlings steal and the Kongs have to recover. 200 are spread across the seven worlds and the DK Isles hub, and there is also a hidden 201st.
Uses: Each world's B. Locker stays shut until you carry enough Golden Bananas, and the number needed is different for every world. Snide also pays one for every blueprint you bring him.
Tips: Each Kong earns five in every world by finishing that Kong's own tasks, 25 in each world. The hidden 201st is larger and carries the Rare logo, and all 201 are needed for 101 percent and the second ending.

sections.name: Blueprint
sections.card:
Summary: Plans for the Blast-o-Matic, which the Kongs have to collect and return to Snide. There are 40 in all, five in every area except Hideout Helm, one for each Kong.
Uses: Snide's H.Q. pays each Kong one Golden Banana for every blueprint that Kong hands in. In Hideout Helm each blueprint also delays the Blast-o-Matic's countdown by a minute.
Tips: A Kasplat guards every blueprint, and its hair colour matches the one Kong who can take it; any other Kong sees only a hologram. The Helm countdown starts at ten minutes and can reach 50 with all 40, and once you have recovered them all Snide lets you replay most of the bonus stages.

sections.name: Crystal Coconut
sections.card:
Summary: A collectable that fuels each Kong's barrel ability. Most levels have a fair number, and they turn up most often where a Kong has to use an ability.
Uses: Crystal Coconuts only start working after a Kong has bought their ability at Cranky's Lab. Strong Kong makes Donkey Kong invincible and lets him cross quicksand and lava, but it ends when the coconuts run out or he uses a Bananaport Pad, and Lanky's OrangSprint burns more coconuts the longer he runs.
Tips: A Kong starts able to carry 20, and each Banana Fairy you catch adds one, up to 40 with all 20 fairies. Catching every fairy also unlocks a cheat in the Mystery menu for unlimited coconuts.

sections.name: Banana Medal
sections.card:
Summary: A brown medal with a banana in its centre; a Kong earns one by picking up 75 bananas of that Kong's own colour in a level.
Uses: There are 40 in all, eight for each Kong, and having 15 lets you play Jetpac in Cranky's Lab. Every medal is needed for 101 percent.
Tips: In Hideout Helm a Kong earns a medal by finishing two Bonus Barrel challenges instead. The five medals there are lost for good if you leave their rooms without collecting them, which ends any chance of 101 percent.

sections.name: Kong weapons (Funky's Store)
sections.card:
Summary: Each Kong buys a personal weapon from Funky Kong for three Banana Bunch Coins: the Coconut Shooter for Donkey, Peanut Popguns for Diddy, the Grape Shooter for Lanky, the Feather Bow for Tiny and the Pineapple Launcher for Chunky.
Uses: A weapon has limited ammo. Donkey's Coconut Shooter shoots Banana Balloons, hits Coconut Switches and snipes enemies from afar, and a Supply Crate gives it five coconuts. Funky's Store, in every level except Hideout Helm, refills any Kong's ammo.
Tips: Every weapon holds up to 50 ammo at first. Ammo Belt 1 (3 coins, from Frantic Factory) raises that to 100, Homing Ammo (5, from Fungi Forest) makes shots home in on enemies, Ammo Belt 2 (5, from Crystal Caves) raises it to 200, and the Sniper Scope (7, from Creepy Castle) lets shots go farther in first-person view.

sections.name: Kong instruments (Candy's Music Shop)
sections.card:
Summary: Each Kong buys an instrument from Candy Kong for three Banana Coins: bongo drums for Donkey, a star-shaped electric guitar for Diddy, a trombone for Lanky, an alto saxophone for Tiny and a triangle for Chunky.
Uses: An instrument can be used ten times at first without a Music Pad, and Candy or Headphones can replenish its energy. The instrument move is one of the ways to defeat Klumps, Kasplats and Zingers.
Tips: Buying the first instrument raises everyone's life bar to two Watermelons. Upgrades raise the uses to 15 (5 coins, from Gloomy Galleon), 20 (7 coins, from Crystal Caves, which also adds a third Watermelon) and 25 (9 coins, from Creepy Castle). Candy's shop is missing from Jungle Japes, Fungi Forest and Hideout Helm.

sections.name: Simian Slam and Kong Switches
sections.card:
Summary: The ground-pound move every Kong learns at Cranky's Lab. It sends out a small shockwave and is mainly used to pound Kong Switches, though it also hurts enemies.
Uses: Green Kong Switches need at least a Simian Slam, blue ones a Super Simian Slam (5 coins, from Fungi Forest) and red ones, found only in Creepy Castle, a Super Duper Simian Slam (7 coins, from Creepy Castle). Each switch shows one Kong's face, and only that Kong can set it off.
Tips: The plain Simian Slam is the only move learned for free. The Super Simian Slam replaces it, and neither upgrade does more damage to enemies than the plain slam. Blue switches start in Fungi Forest, with one exception: one sits in Gloomy Galleon's lobby on DK Isles.

sections.name: Cranky's Lab potions
sections.card:
Summary: Cranky Kong's potions teach the Kongs special attacks and abilities for Banana Bunch Coins, from the free Simian Slam to Hunky Chunky. Cranky's Lab is in all the levels except Hideout Helm.
Uses: Each Kong has three abilities that cost 3, 5 and 7 coins in turn. Donkey: Baboon Blast, Strong Kong, Gorilla Grab. Diddy: Chimpy Charge, Rocketbarrel Boost, Simian Spring. Lanky: OrangStand, Baboon Balloon, OrangSprint. Tiny: Mini-Monkey, Pony Tail Twirl, Monkeyport. Chunky: Hunky Chunky, Primate Punch, Gorilla Gone.
Tips: Each Kong's first potion is on sale from a set world: Donkey's and Diddy's from Jungle Japes, Lanky's and Tiny's from Angry Aztec, Chunky's from Frantic Factory. Strong Kong is switched on by jumping into a Donkey Barrel and OrangSprint by jumping into a Lanky Barrel.
